title: Staff / Principal Engineer Expectations
content: Staff and Principal Engineer roles expect candidates who operate as architectural leaders with organization-wide technical influence. Evidence must demonstrate: defining technical direction and system design across multiple teams or domains, driving engineering standards and best practices, mentoring senior engineers, making technology adoption decisions at org scale, and delivering long-horizon technical roadmaps. Staff-level impact is measured in months-to-years of architectural influence, not sprint velocity.

title: Senior Engineer Expectations
content: Senior Engineer roles expect full technical autonomy within a domain or team. Evidence must demonstrate: designing and implementing complex features end-to-end with minimal supervision, making independent architectural decisions for team-scoped systems, reviewing and guiding junior/mid engineer work, proactively identifying and resolving technical debt, and delivering production systems with measurable reliability and performance outcomes.

title: Lead / Tech Lead Expectations
content: Tech Lead roles combine individual technical contribution with team coordination and delivery accountability. Evidence must demonstrate: technical leadership over a small team (3-8 engineers), hands-on code contribution alongside coordination responsibilities, sprint planning and unblocking team members, cross-functional collaboration with product and design, and ownership of technical delivery timelines.

title: Mid-Level Engineer Expectations
content: Mid-level / intermediate engineers are expected to work independently on well-defined tasks, contribute meaningfully to feature development, participate in code reviews, and demonstrate growth toward senior-level responsibilities. Evidence should show increasing scope of work over time, ability to implement complete features with moderate guidance, and participation in system design discussions.

title: Junior Engineer Expectations
content: Junior engineers are expected to learn, contribute to well-specified tasks, and grow under senior guidance. Evidence criteria for junior roles should be adjusted: project-level experience, academic projects, bootcamp graduates, open source contributions, and internships are all acceptable evidence. Keyword presence in a skills list carries more weight than for senior roles due to limited professional experience available.

title: Management Role vs. IC Role Distinction
content: Management roles (Engineering Manager, Director) require evidence of people management, performance reviews, hiring decisions, and team organizational design — not only technical contributions. Individual Contributor (IC) roles with 'influence' language (e.g., 'shape the technical direction') require technical influence through code, design, and review — not organizational management. Do not conflate management signals with IC technical leadership evidence.
